neighbours.label: hedged or hypothetical framing ('in an ideal world ... would', 'under normal conditions ... might', 'some might see this as'); the - pole is the factual side ('in fact', 'strictly speaking')
fire: In a perfect world, every patient would see a doctor within a day.
Under ordinary circumstances, the ferry might cross in forty minutes.
Some critics might see this as a weak ending to the series.
In an ideal world, all trains would arrive exactly on time.
Under different circumstances, the players might have panicked.
Many parents might view this as an unfair change to the rules.
In a perfect world, nobody would have to work two jobs to pay rent.
Under normal conditions, the plants might flower by early June.
quiet: In practice, most patients see a doctor within about a week.
On Tuesday, the ferry crossed in forty minutes despite the wind.
In fact, critics praised the ending as the best part of the series.
In reality, many trains arrived late during the winter months.
During the match, the players stayed calm and kept the ball.
Most parents welcomed the change to the rules at the meeting.
Today, many people work two jobs to pay the rent in this city.
This year, the plants flowered in early June as usual.

notes: Probe: 'In an ideal world, ... would' 0.32, 'Some readers might see this as' 0.33, 'Under normal conditions, ... might' 0.26; the past counterfactual 'Had ..., could have' 0.11; factual contrasts 0.01-0.13 ('Strictly speaking' 0.13). Fire items stay close to the scoring frames.
